cards.explanation: The answer is False. David says, “apart from You I have no good thing.” Not a few, not one. I think that's about the most honest line anybody can say to God, friends, and it fits in a single breath.

The answer is the saints in the land. David says, “As for the saints in the land, they are the excellence in whom all my delight resides.” He names the saints in the land as the ones he delights in. That's a good kind of friend group, bakers.

The answer is their sorrows. David says, “Sorrows will multiply to those who chase other gods.” Notice what's multiplying, friends, and it's not a good batch. I'd take one tray of plain dough over a hundred trays of that.
The answer is True. David says he will not “…speak their names with my lips.” He's not saying it quietly or with an eye roll, friends. He just keeps those names off his lips, and that's a firm line.

The answer is the LORD. David says, “The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; You have made my lot secure.” Out of everything he could pick, he picks the LORD. When the Giver is your portion, bakers, you're not worried about the size of the slice.
The answer is False. David says, “surely my inheritance is delightful.” He looks at the lines of his boundary and calls them pleasant places. I think that's a man who's glad where he landed, friends.
The answer is that He counsels him. David says, “I will bless the LORD who counsels me…” He even adds that “even at night my conscience instructs me.” Free advice that doesn't sleep, friends.

The answer is that he will not be shaken. David says, “I have set the LORD always before me. Because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.” Steady hands, bakers, and that's coming from a stamper with a mustache for arms.

The answers are glad and securely. David says, “…my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices…” and then, “my body also will dwell securely.” His joy comes right out of his mouth, friends, and you can't keep that quiet. Not nervously, not by luck. Securely.

The answer is False. David says God will not “…let Your Holy One see decay.” Peter, one of Jesus' apostles, later says David looked ahead and spoke about the resurrection of the Christ (Acts 2:31). Big promise, friends, tucked inside one short line.

The answer is the path of life. David says, “You have made known to me the path of life…” After talking about Sheol and decay, he turns to life, friends. Then he adds, “You will fill me with joy in Your presence…”
